c54f20dbe76ac8b3411ad21e0ed7deea6f0cfd4d 2026-08-14 20:41:42 +1200

Vendored from https://github.com/smartalock/wireguard-lwip at the commit
above. Taken directly rather than out of MicroLink (the ESP32 Tailscale
client that prompted this), because MicroLink vendors this same code and we
want neither Tailscale nor FreeRTOS -- only the WireGuard layer, hooked
straight to lwIP.

What was taken:  src/{wireguard,wireguardif,crypto}.{c,h},
                 src/wireguard-platform.h, src/crypto/refc/*
What was left:   src/crypto/cortex/* -- Cortex-M0 Thumb-1 assembly for
                 X25519. This part is a Cortex-M33, and X25519 runs once per
                 handshake (every ~2 minutes), so portable C costs nothing
                 worth the risk of hand-written assembly for the wrong core.
                 example/ -- an lwIP port we do not use.

Local changes: TWO, in src/wireguardif.c (+ declarations in wireguardif.h).

  1. Where it delivered a decrypted
               packet with ip_input(pbuf, device->netif) it now calls
               device->netif->input(pbuf, device->netif). netif->input is
               lwIP's documented entry point and what its own drivers use;
               calling ip_input() directly skips whatever the port installed
               there. For us that was the receive byte counter, so a tunnel
               that was demonstrably carrying traffic reported rx_bytes 0
               for its whole life -- and wg.status is the only way to
               diagnose the tunnel remotely, so a status that under-reports
               a healthy tunnel is worse than no status.

  2. Uplink selection (src/net/uplink.c). The outer UDP used plain
               udp_sendto(), so it always left through lwIP's default route.
               It now goes through wg_udp_send(): udp_sendto_if_src() on the
               interface set by wireguardif_set_tx_netif(), with that
               interface's address as the source (falling back to the old
               call when none is set, or it is down). Plus
               wireguardif_send_keepalive_now(), so the server roams to a
               new uplink on the first authenticated packet after a switch
               instead of at the next 25 s keepalive. The receive side is
               unchanged: the pcb is bound to ANY, so the old interface keeps
               receiving during the switch (make-before-break).

               Search for "LOCAL CHANGE" to find them when rebasing.

The platform hooks that wireguard-platform.h declares are implemented in
src/net/wg.c.
